Cowpens. On January 17, 1781, American General Daniel Morgan defeated British cavalry colonel Banastre Tarleton at the Cowpens in South Carolina. Morgan's tactical use of militia and cavalry was masterful: he positioned them to trade fire then retreat behind Continental regulars. This maneuver trapped Tarleton's charge and shattered the British attack, forcing the surrender of nearly 800 troops. The numbers tell the story. The British lost approximately 850 men killed, wounded, or captured, while American casualties were fewer than 80. Tarleton's cavalry charge, a signature tactic for the British in the South, was decisively broken. Morgan's victory reinvigorated American resistance in the Carolinas and led to a series of American gains in the South. Called one of the finest tactical battles of the entire war, it was perfectly suited to the terrain and the opposing forces. It helped set conditions for the American victory at Guilford Courthouse just two months later and the eventual British withdrawal from the Carolinas.
